region.text: the lands of the three Leagues

ledger.note: 1471: the Three Leagues unite. 'In 1471 an alliance gave birth to the Three Leagues' (Graubünden page); the Three Leagues page says joint meetings are 'evidenced from 1461' and links date to 1471, 'but there is no documentary proof of this date'; the Bundesbrief of 23 September 1524 followed ('the Three Leagues remained a loose association until' then). The League of God's House (1367), the Grey League (1395) and the League of the Ten Jurisdictions (1436) have no dossiers; they are the Leagues' parts. The page names Graubünden's valleys, not a boundary.

region.text: the Three Leagues, associate of the Old Swiss Confederacy

ledger.note: 1497: the Three Leagues become associates of the Old Swiss Confederacy. Old Swiss Confederacy page: the Three Leagues 'became an associates of the Old Swiss Confederacy in 1497/98 through the events of the Swabian War' (swiss-confederation /ledger/19 puts the Grey League in 1497 and the others in 1498). Mirror of that event; the Leagues stay sovereign, so the tint is the nearest rule-4 status, not subjection. Confidence 2: the page gives 1497/98, the first year is taken.

1512: the Leagues take the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio. The Old Swiss Confederacy page lists 'Bormio (1512-1797)', 'Chiavenna (1512-1797)' and 'Valtellina (1512-1797)'; the Valtellina page says 'Throughout the 16th, 17th, and 18th centuries, the Valtellina belonged to the Three Leagues'; the Chiavenna page says the town 'was conquered by the Leagues's forces during the War of the League of Cambrai' (it links the conquest to the 1513 Battle of Novara, so the 1512 of the Swiss table is the only year any page gives). Neither page narrates the taking. Repair 2026-11-01: the counterpart was the Duchy of Milan; it is the Kingdom of France, which held the Milanese 1499-1512 (duchy-of-milan /ledger/17 loses the duchy to France in 1499, and its 1512 regain, /ledger/18, excludes the Valtellina; swiss-confederation /ledger/25 notes that Cliopatria's 1510 holder of the Sondrio cells is the Kingdom of France). The Chiavenna page adds that the Sforza, the Visconti's successors, had fought the Leagues over the area, so a Sforza claim stood behind the French holding.

region.text: the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio, subject territory of the Three Leagues and so tinted with them

ledger.note: 1512: the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio become subject territory of the Three Leagues, the Confederacy's associate. Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/25. Old Swiss Confederacy page: the three are listed '(1512-1797)' among the territories that were 'separate subjects of cantons or associates'; they were never associates themselves, so the tint is the Leagues' own. Pairs with the 1620 end and the 1639 resumption below.

region.text: the Valtellina, taken out of the Three Leagues

ledger.note: July 1620: the Valtellina rises against the Leagues. 'On the evening of 18/19 July 1620, a force of Valtellina rebels' marched into Tirano and the attack 'took the Valtellina out of the Three Leagues'; the Valtellina page adds the rebels were 'supported by Austrian and Italian troops'. The Valtellina War page says 'the Spanish incited a revolt in Valtelline and eventually controlled the valley'.

July 1620: the Valtellina War begins ('Date: July 1620 - 5 March 1626'). Spain 'eventually controlled the valley'; France, the Three Leagues, Venice and Savoy fought Spain, the Empire, Genoa, the papacy and Grisons rebels. Spain is the researcher's choice of the one state the blend names.

region.text: the Valtellina, taken out of the Three Leagues

ledger.note: July 1620: the Valtellina leaves the Three Leagues and so the associate's tint. 'On the evening of 18/19 July 1620, a force of Valtellina rebels' attacked and 'took the Valtellina out of the Three Leagues' (Graubünden page). Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/33, same month as the loss above.

region.text: the Müstair, the Lower Engadine and Prättigau valleys

ledger.note: January 1622: the Leagues cede three valleys. 'The resulting peace treaty of January 1622, forced Grisons to cede the Müstair, the Lower Engadine and Prättigau valleys.' The page does not name the recipient; later 'Treaties with Austria in 1649 and 1652' bring two valleys back, so the Habsburg monarchy is taken as the holder.

5 March 1626: the Treaty of Monzón ends the war. It 'granted the Valtelline self-rule guaranteed by the Papacy, Spain, and France'; 'The Grisons and Valtelline Protestants received nothing.' The Valtellina stays outside the Leagues until 1639.

region.text: the Valtellina brought back under League sovereignty

ledger.note: 3 September 1639: the Valtellina returns to the Leagues. 'On 3 September 1639 the Leagues agreed with Spain to bring the Valtellina back under League sovereignty.' The Valtellina and Valtellina War pages do not mention 1639.

region.text: the Valtellina brought back under League sovereignty

ledger.note: 3 September 1639: the Valtellina returns to the Three Leagues and the tint resumes. 'On 3 September 1639 the Leagues agreed with Spain to bring the Valtellina back under League sovereignty' (Graubünden page). Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/34.

1649: Prättigau back in the Leagues (bridging date inside a page range). League of the Ten Jurisdictions page: 'The rights to High Justice were held by the Dukes of Austria, until the League bought these rights from the duke in 1649-1652' (infobox: 'All Ten Jurisdictions free from Austria: 1649-1652'); the same page says the Count of Matsch, who held the lower Prättigau, sold his rights to Austria in 1477. The Prättigau is the heart of the Ten Jurisdictions, but the page does not name a year for the valley alone, so 1649, the start of the range, is a bridging date (confidence 1). The Bündner Wirren page adds that 'in 1622, the Prättigau valley rebelled against the Austrians and drove them out of the valley'; the Austrian rights nevertheless lasted until the buyout, so the valley stays out of the Leagues' sovereignty 1622-1648 here. Repair 2026-11-01: source changed from the Graubünden page (which is silent on the Prättigau) to the Ten Jurisdictions page.

1652: the Lower Engadine buys its freedom from Austria. Scuol page (chief town of the Lower Engadine): 'In 1621/1622 the village was devastated by Austrian troops; in 1652 it bought its freedom from Austria.' The Graubünden page says 'Treaties with Austria in 1649 and 1652, brought the Müstair and Lower Engadine valleys back' without assigning years; the Scuol page dates the Lower Engadine. Confidence 2: the year is the page's for the village of Scuol, the valley-wide region is my reading. Repair 2026-11-01: this event stood at 1649 (confidence 2) as the first of the two treaties; the Engadin page is silent on the buyout.

1652 (bridging): the Müstair valley comes back from Austria. The Graubünden page says 'Treaties with Austria in 1649 and 1652, brought the Müstair and Lower Engadine valleys back' and does not say which valley in which year; the Val Müstair page does not mention Austria at all. The Müstair valley is dated with the Lower Engadine, whose buyout is 1652 on the Scuol page, because the Graubünden page groups the two; the year is not dated for the valley by any page. Repair 2026-11-01: it stood at 1649.

region.text: the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio, annexed to the Cisalpine Republic

ledger.note: October 1797: the Valtellina joins the Cisalpine Republic. The districts 'were annexed to the Cisalpine Republic on 10 October 1797', 'having permanently been detached from the Leagues after Revolutionary France fomented revolt there'; the Valtellina page agrees ('On 10 October 1797, the French supported a revolt'). The Cisalpine Republic dossier gives 22 October for the announcement.

region.text: the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio, annexed to the Cisalpine Republic

ledger.note: 10 October 1797: the Valtellina leaves the Three Leagues and the tint ends. 'The districts were annexed to the Cisalpine Republic on 10 October 1797' (Three Leagues page). Mirror of swiss-confederation /ledger/36.

1798: the Three Leagues cease to be associates of the Confederacy because the Confederacy fell to the French invasion of March 1798 (Old Swiss Confederacy page: 'The Swiss Confederacy fell to a French invasion in 1798, after which it became the short-lived Helvetic Republic'). Month 3 and the year follow swiss-confederation /ledger/40, whose owner rounds the end to the collapse; the page gives the year only. The Leagues themselves lasted to 21 April 1799 (the loss and dissolve events below), about thirteen months as an unassociated state.

region.text: the Three Leagues, the canton of Raetia

ledger.note: 21 April 1799: the Three Leagues join the Helvetic Republic. Infobox 'Annexed to the Helvetic Republic: 21 April 1799'; 'the Three Leagues were absorbed into the Helvetic Republic' as the canton of Raetia. The Graubünden page puts the absorption in 1798.

region.text: the Three Leagues, the canton of Raetia

ledger.note: 1799: the Three Leagues end. The canton of Raetia of the Helvetic Republic; 'under the Act of Mediation' the Leagues 'were incorporated into a restored Swiss Confederacy' as the canton of Graubünden in 1803 (Graubünden page).

wars.name: Swabian War
wars.outcome: 'The Habsburgs were defeated at Calven Gorge and Dornach'; the Leagues sided with the Confederacy. No border change on the page.
wars.note: The page gives the year only as 'three years later' than the Habsburg acquisition of Toggenburg possessions 'in 1496', i.e. 1499.

wars.name: Bündner Wirren

zones.text: the Müstair, the Lower Engadine and Prättigau valleys

wars.outcome: 'Between 1618 and 1639 it became a battleground between competing factions': the Valtellina left the Leagues in July 1620 and returned on 3 September 1639; the Müstair, Lower Engadine and Prättigau were ceded in January 1622, the Prättigau came back within 1649-1652 (Ten Jurisdictions page) and the Lower Engadine in 1652 (Scuol page), the Müstair with it ('Treaties with Austria in 1649 and 1652').

wars.name: Valtellina War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Monzón, 5 March 1626: the Valtelline got self-rule guaranteed by the Papacy, Spain and France; Spain and France had equal passage rights; 'The Grisons and Valtelline Protestants received nothing.'
wars.note: On 24 November 1624 French troops entered the Valtellina through Poschiavo and expelled the papal troops; in March 1625 Lesdiguières and the Duke of Savoy drove Genoese and Spanish forces from some positions.

certainty.note: Alpine valley jurisdictions and league boundaries, none surveyed on the pages opened; the Valtellina frontier with Milan is the same.

Sharp from the 1649-1652 treaties with Austria that fixed the Prättigau, Müstair and Lower Engadine (the last of them in 1652); the page gives no survey line, so this rests on those treaties and on the long-settled valley jurisdictions.

notes: No Cliopatria row: every keyframe is new. The three Leagues before 1471 (God's House 1367, Grey League 1395, Ten Jurisdictions 1436) are parts of this state, not predecessors with dossiers. The union year 1471 is Graubünden's wording (the Ten Jurisdictions page agrees: 'In 1471 the League allied with the Grey League, forming the Three Leagues'); the Three Leagues page says 'no documentary proof' and the Bundesbrief of 23 September 1524 is the later formal date. Valtellina 1512: the holder was the Kingdom of France (1499-1512), not the Duchy of Milan; kingdom-of-france /ledger/79 sends all of Lombardy to the Duchy in 1512 and should except Sondrio and add a 1512 loss of it to three-leagues; duchy-of-milan /ledger/18 already excludes the Valtellina. Valtellina 1620-1639: the pages give a rebel regime, Spanish control and papal-guaranteed self-rule after 1626; neither kingdom-of-spain nor state-of-milan has a matching gain, so the valley may render as nobody's. The French occupations (the Valtellina War page: French troops enter on 24 November 1624; Rohan's campaigns 1631-1637 on the Bündner Wirren and Rohan pages) are not in the ledger because the pages opened disagree and give no dates for their end ('In 1627 the French withdrew', Bündner Wirren page, against the Treaty of Monzón of 5 March 1626 on the Valtellina War page; the Rohan page dates neither entry nor withdrawal). Associate tint: the vassal events mirror swiss-confederation /ledger/19 (1497), 25 (1512), 33 (July 1620), 34 (September 1639), 36 (October 1797) and 40 (1798-03); the Leagues are the associate, and the Valtellina is the Leagues' subject land, tinted with them. The Leagues' own end is 21 April 1799 (infobox), thirteen months after the associate tint ends. Three Austrian valleys: the Prättigau comes back inside the 1649-1652 range (Ten Jurisdictions page; 1649 bridging, confidence 1), the Lower Engadine in 1652 (Scuol page, confidence 2) and the Müstair with it (Graubünden page groups the two valleys, confidence 1). habsburg-monarchy has no January 1622 gain of the three valleys and no 1649/1652 losses. The valleys are coordinate circles (the gazetteer has no Prättigau, Lower Engadine or Müstair). Gazetteer names needed: Prättigau, Lower Engadine (Unterengadin), Müstair, Valtellina.
